D: An uptight FBI agent and a foul-mouthed Boston detective team up to take down a drug lord.
P: Serve the mains at the Mullins family dinner.
S: Boston clam chowder with oyster crackers

Creamy New England clam chowder with smoky bacon, potato and fresh clams, served in mugs with crisp oyster crackers and chives. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon until crisp, then add 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml fish stock and 300g diced potato and simmer 12 minutes. Add 1kg cleaned clams or vongole, cover and cook 4 minutes until open, then pick out the shells. Stir in 300ml thickened cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers and chives.
Mullins stopping a runner with a watermelon

Oven-crisped chicken wings tossed in buttery buffalo hot sauce, served with a chunky blue cheese dip and cold celery sticks. Pat 1.2kg chicken wings dry and toss with 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. Bake on a rack at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and toss the wings through it. For the dip, mash 100g blue cheese with 150g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with celery sticks.
M: Mullins family roast beef and gravy

Garlic and mustard crusted roast beef sliced pink, with crunchy roast potatoes, honey carrots and a rich pan gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 crushed garlic cloves, oil and salt. Parboil 1.2kg quartered potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, rough up and toss in 3 tbsp oil. Roast the beef at 200C for 1 hour for medium rare with the potatoes on a separate tray. Add 4 halved carrots tossed in 1 tbsp honey for the last 35 minutes. Rest the beef 15 minutes. Whisk 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 400ml beef stock and simmer to a gravy.
W: a Boston classic for a Boston film

Two layers of light butter sponge filled with thick vanilla pastry cream and covered in a glossy dark chocolate glaze. Whisk 3 egg yolks, 60g caster sugar and 2 tbsp cornflour, then whisk in 300ml hot milk. Return to the pan and stir until thick, add 1 tsp vanilla and chill. Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, then 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Bake in a 20cm tin at 180C for 30 minutes and cool. Split in half and fill with the custard. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream and pour over the top.
K: two cops who can't stand each other, at first

Irish whiskey shaken hard with fresh lemon, sugar syrup and egg white until frothy, served over ice with a cherry and a dash of bitters. For each drink, add 60ml Irish whiskey, 30ml fresh lemon juice, 20ml sugar syrup and 1 egg white to a shaker or jar. Shake hard without ice for 15 seconds, then add ice and shake again for 15 seconds. Strain into a short glass over fresh ice. Top the foam with 2 dashes of aromatic bitters and drop in a cocktail cherry. Repeat for 4 drinks.
